source.title: Positively Scale-Invariant Flatness of ReLU Neural Networks
source.authors: Ming-Yang Yi; Qi Meng; Wei Chen; Zhi-Ming Ma; Tie-Yan Liu

record.file_problem: Text is the full paper, including appendix; no apparent truncation or garbling affecting the reported results.
record.tranche_reason: The paper measures flatness in basis-path space and relates it to test performance, using a different flatness measure from the versions listed.
record.gate_note: The paper's own empirical result compares two CIFAR-10 models trained with different batch sizes. Prior-work results mentioned in the text are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: Section 6 directly compares held-out accuracy across SGD batch sizes, bearing on V5 using the same basic method and measure. However, it does not establish equal epoch budgets. Its basis-path flatness results do not measure V7's magnitude-aware weight sharpness.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's empirical paraphrase is accurate but incomplete. The authors also prove positive scale invariance of their basis-path flatness definitions and derive a PAC-Bayes connection and a conditional upper bound. Their empirical evidence consists of two models and qualitative landscape plots.
record.recipe_differences: Introduces and visualizes flatness in basis-path-value space; the claim versions concern random-label memorization, width, architecture, optimizer, batch size, dropout, magnitude-aware sharpness, or memorized-example removal.
record.method_sensitivity: The two tested batch sizes (128 and 2048) produce different test accuracies and qualitatively different PSI-flatness landscapes.

fits_no_version.finding: The higher-accuracy model has a qualitatively flatter loss landscape under Gaussian perturbations of basis-path values.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For these two PlainNet-18 models, greater robustness to basis-path perturbations coincides with higher test accuracy.

fits_no_version.finding: Theorems 3.1–3.2 show that non-invariant weight-flatness measures can change under positive rescaling while network predictions remain identical.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Weight-flatness measures that lack positive scale invariance cannot uniquely characterize generalization across equivalent ReLU parameterizations.

record.problems: The empirical comparison covers two models and one dataset; the flatness comparison is qualitative and shown in figures, with no uncertainty reported.
record.rows_left_out: No additional own-result rows identified. Related optimizer and flatness findings in the related-work discussion are cited prior work.

untested.parts: Test error as width increases beyond interpolation.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizers and tuning-dependent differences.
Whether the batch penalty holds under equal epoch budgets; workload-dependent thresholds and adaptations that remove the penalty.
Dropout and its interactions with dataset size, augmentation and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware weight perturbations, their ranking of generalization gaps, and comparisons with norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for these versions. Its theoretical critique concerns non-invariant weight-flatness definitions and does not establish a failure of V7's particular magnitude-aware measure. No numerical PSI-flatness values, repeated-run uncertainty, or explicit epoch budgets are supplied.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Width sweep beyond the interpolation threshold.
Large-batch effects under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and comparison against norm- and margin-based measures.

rows.subject: stacked deep CNN-PlainNet-18
rows.operation_detail: Visualized loss landscape in basis-path-value space around the trained model using two random directions.
rows.measure: PSI-flatness, described qualitatively through the loss landscape; test accuracy
rows.note: The paper states that the better-accuracy model lies in a flatter region, but provides no numerical PSI-flatness value.
rows.check: For the batch-size comparison, this is the small-batch baseline: 87.78% accuracy, or 12.22% test error. Both models reach training loss below 0.001. Equal epoch budgets are not stated. The qualitative PSI-flatness component fits no version.

rows.subject: stacked deep CNN-PlainNet-18
rows.operation_detail: Visualized loss landscape in basis-path-value space around the trained model using two random directions.
rows.measure: PSI-flatness, described qualitatively through the loss landscape; test accuracy
rows.note: The paper states that this model lies in a less-flat region than the batch-size-128 model; no numerical PSI-flatness value is reported.
rows.check: Use R1 as the accuracy baseline: batch size 2048 achieves 86.3% accuracy, or 13.7% test error, a 1.48 percentage-point penalty. Both models reach training loss below 0.001. Equal epoch budgets are not stated. The qualitative PSI-flatness component fits no version.

relationships.condition: PlainNet-18 on CIFAR-10 with SGD, batch sizes 128 versus 2048; epoch-budget equivalence unverified.
relationships.reason: R1 and R2 show 87.78% versus 86.3% test accuracy despite both training losses being below 0.001; this supports the batch-penalty component but does not establish its fixed-epoch condition.
relationships.display_finding: Unverified results suggest lower test accuracy at the larger batch despite similarly low training losses, without establishing equal epoch budgets.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
